name: Element.makeelement
reason: CopyIndependentPy only says the original's attributes are unchanged after setting one on the copy, so a makeelement that returns an element with no attributes satisfies it; that the copy has the original's attributes is not stated.

name: Element.__copy__
reason: copyPy omits elem.text/elem.tail and elem[:] = self (:191-193, which iterates self through __getitem__ and type-checks each child), and the property passes for a copy that loses its attributes.

name: Element.__getitem__
reason: The body is self._children[index], modelled by the list model's getitem and slice, and ItemTwins and GetSliceTwins prove it equal to the C accelerator for every int and every slice.

name: Element.__setitem__
reason: setItemPy and setSlicePy mirror the type-check loop and then the list store, one-shot iterator exhaustion included; ItemTwins and SetSliceTwinsSeq are proven, and the order and iterator divergences are refuted with a bug.

name: Element.__delitem__
reason: del self._children[index] goes through the list model, and ItemTwins and DelSliceCIsList prove it equal to the C accelerator for every int and every slice.

name: Element.append
reason: WritersTwins assumes T.isElem x, so the _assert_is_element TypeError in this body (:230) never runs, and an append without the check still satisfies it.

name: Element.extend
reason: extendPy checks and appends item by item with a fallible, re-entrant iterator; WritersTwins covers lists with non-Elements and extendTwins_refuted records the atomicity divergence.

name: Element.insert

name: Element._assert_is_element
reason: typeErrPy mirrors the isinstance check and the message, and itemStoreTwins_refuted runs it (TypeError before IndexError), with bug textlibs-etree-py-twin-setitem.

name: Element.remove
reason: The citation 'ElementTree.py:247-270' in EtreeRemove.lean points at _assert_is_element and part of remove, but 3.15.2's remove is :254-274; the model itself (list.remove, then the ValueError conversion) matches the body.
